papers.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

papers.title: The symplectic isotopy problem for rational cuspidal curves
papers.abstract: We define a suitably tame class of singular symplectic curves in 4-manifolds, namely those whose singularities are modeled on complex curve singularities. We study the corresponding symplectic isotopy problem, with a focus on rational curves with irreducible singularities (rational cuspidal curves) in the complex projective plane. We prove that every such curve is isotopic to a complex curve in degrees up to 5, and for curves with one singularity whose link is a torus knot. Classification results of symplectic isotopy classes rely on pseudo-holomorphic curves together with a symplectic version of birational geometry of log pairs and techniques from 4-dimensional topology.

papers.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
papers.abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We prove that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\left\lfloor4(n-1)/3\right\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings.

papers.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
papers.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Z\'u\~niga, are given.

papers.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation in which the image of every codimension one face is a subcomplex. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.

papers.title: Restricted (2+1)-TQFTs supported by thickened and solid tori
papers.abstract: A faithful $(1+1)$ TQFT has recently been constructed, but the existence of a faithful $(2+1)$ TQFT remains an open question, that subsumes the hard problem of linearity of mapping class groups of surfaces. To circumvent the latter problem we construct a subcategory of the category of 3-cobordisms, containing disjoint unions of tori and simplest cobordisms between them. On this we define TQFTs that are able to distinguish pairs of torus bundles and lens spaces, previously shown not to be distinguishable by quantum invariants.

papers.title: An infinity-categorical TQFT from instantons
papers.abstract: In this paper, we lift the instanton TQFT from ordinary categories to the $\infty$-categorical setting by constructing a functor $CI:\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}\longrightarrow\mathsf{D}$ from an $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ for instantons to an $\infty$-derived category $\mathsf{D}$ of $2$-periodic chain complexes. The construction of $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ is a modification of the $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{Bord}_4$ introduced by Lurie and by Calaque--Scheimbauer using complete Segal spaces. The target $\infty$-category $\mathsf{D}$ is obtained via the dg nerve of the dg category of $2$-periodic chain complexes of finitely presented projective $\mathbb{Z}$-modules. The information encoded by the functor $CI$ was already developed by Kronheimer--Mrowka using families of metrics on cobordisms. Our reinterpretation in terms of $\infty$-categories conceptually simplifies the construction of the hypercube complexes underlying the link spectral sequence. This viewpoint also clarifies hyperbox complexes and compression in Manolescu--Ozsv\'{a}th's work, and possible $A_\infty$-structures, especially their signs and higher coherence. In addition, we lift the generalized cap product $\mu$-operators in instanton Floer homology to the chain level and construct explicit homotopies and higher homotopies establishing the commutativity of multiple $\mu$-operators in even degrees.

papers.title: Geometry of Unimodular Random Hyperbolic Polyhedra
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric and probabilistic theory of unimodular random infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$, allowing ordinary, ideal, and hyperideal vertices. Our results relate local dihedral geometry to global conformal type and random-walk behavior. A central role is played by a geometric characteristic $L_f(P)$, determined by the dihedral angles incident to a face $f$. We establish the unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity $$ \mathbb E[L_f(P)]=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathbb E[deg(f)]. $$ Together with circle-pattern uniformization, this yields a sharp parabolic-hyperbolic dichotomy governed by the expected geometric characteristic. We also introduce polyhedral soficity and prove that admissible Benjamini-Schramm limits of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra are parabolic. We further establish a quantitative Ring Lemma for regular circle patterns, providing degree-sensitive geometric control without assuming bounded degrees. Combined with unimodular probability methods, this estimate enables us to identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Our results extend the geometric-characteristic theory beyond ideal polyhedra, connecting three-dimensional geometry, unimodular Gauss-Bonnet theory, and stochastic boundary behavior.

papers.title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
papers.abstract: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

papers.title: Injectivity and continuity of the intersection form in infinite type
papers.abstract: We study two fundamental properties of the intersection pairing between geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces which are classical in the finite-type closed setting: injectivity of the marked length spectrum and continuity of the intersection form. We show that geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces of the first kind are determined by their intersection numbers with closed curves, extending Otal's marked length spectrum rigidity argument from finite-type to infinite-type surfaces. In contrast, we prove that the intersection pairing is not continuous in general for the natural topologies by constructing explicit counterexamples. We then prove sufficient criteria for continuity of intersection numbers for infinite-type surfaces.

papers.title: A homological approach to Dax invariants
papers.abstract: We present a homological construction of Dax invariants in 4-manifolds that is intrinsic to the topological category and requires neither smoothing nor generic representatives. Applications include an extension of the invariant of Cha-Kim to neat disks without assuming local flatness, and a topological definition of the Dax map for arc spaces that yields a short alternative proof of the topological Dax isomorphism theorem.

papers.title: Euler characteristic and flat cohomology of convex projective $4$-manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $M=\Omega/\Gamma$ be a closed properly convex real projective $4$-manifold. We prove the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture for this class of manifolds, i.e. $\chi(M)\geq0$. The argument transfers Akagawa's double-form identity on the Cheng--Yau cone over $\Omega$ to a Bochner identity on $M$, from which we deduce that $H^q(M;\Lambda^pE^*)=0$ whenever $q<p(n+1-p)/(n+1)$, in arbitrary dimension $n$, for some flat bundle $E$ naturally attached to $M$. In dimension four, this implies that the cohomology with coefficients in $\Lambda^2E^*$ concentrates in degree two.

papers.title: On the Concordance Invariants of Cable Links
papers.abstract: We study the Beliakova--Wehrli link $s$-invariant and Cavallo's link $\tau$-invariant of coherently oriented cables. For knots satisfying extremal four-ball genus and maximal self-linking hypotheses, we establish bounds for the $s$-invariant of $(p,q)$-cables, where $p$ and $q$ are not necessarily coprime, and show that these bounds are sharp under certain conditions. For the $\tau$-invariant, we prove analogous bounds for arbitrary companion knots and exact formulas whenever $\tau(K)=\pm g_4(K)\ne 0$. Specializing to the coherently oriented cable links associated to an $n$-framed knot, we apply these bounds to the lasagna $s$-invariant of Ren and Willis. The resulting applications provide upper bounds for the lasagna $s$-invariant of knot traces and a criterion for distinguishing homeomorphic zero traces up to orientation-preserving diffeomorphism.

papers.title: Spin and scalar curvature on punctured four manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that a closed spin four-manifold with nonzero signature, even after being punctured along a finite graph, does not admit a complete metric with uniformly positive scalar curvature. We also show that this implies Schoen's conjecture on $L^{\infty}$-metrics with non-negative scalar curvature for these manifolds. This is in contrast to higher dimensions. A key new observation, which could be of independent interest, is that Gromov's $\mu$-bubbles are a convenient class of boundaries for the APS boundary value problem for the Dirac operator.

papers.title: A new formulation of the Teichm\"uller TQFT
papers.abstract: Using the Weil--Gel'fand--Zak transform of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm, we construct a compact state integral for positively shaped triangulations of oriented pseudo three-manifolds. The integral is labelled by a circle-valued first cohomology class of the vertex complement (a ``sector'') and takes boundary values in a line bundle over compatible boundary cocycles. We prove absolute convergence, smoothness, invariance under shape gauge transformations and under compatible shaped $2$--$3$ moves, branching independence, and a single-valued global meromorphic continuation in all shape and boundary parameters for each fixed quantum parameter. Gluing is expressed by a conditional Haar integral which retains the final cohomology class; the ordinary trace of integrated cut amplitudes computes an average of the sectors over a torus of classes determined by the cut, and is a sewing formula for every cut of a closed oriented three-manifold, but not for arbitrary pseudo-manifolds. For closed admissible triangulations, the original Teichm\"uller partition function is the normalized average of the sectors; this yields its global meromorphic continuation. A translation law relates sectors differing by twice an extending class, with phases given by linking pairings; for closed three-manifolds the sectors are supported in a distinguished coset of twice the torsion group and are determined by a single amplitude, which a nonvanishing twisted quadratic Gauss sum recovers from the original partition function.

papers.title: Spherical growth of reciprocal classes in the Hecke Groups
papers.abstract: Let $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, $r>2$, and let $\Gamma_{2r} \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}) \ast (\mathbb{Z}/2r\mathbb{Z})$ be the Hecke group. Let $\mathcal{N}_\ell$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of reciprocal elements with cyclically reduced word length exactly $\ell$ in the standard generating set of $\Gamma_{2r}$. Let $P(x)$ be the polynomial \[ P(x) = x^{r+1} - 2\sum_{i=1}^{r-1} x^{i} - 1. \] Let $\rho$ be the unique positive root of $P$ and $C$ be a constant depending on $r.$ We prove that, as $\ell \to \infty$, \[|\mathcal{N}_\ell| \sim C\rho^{\left\lfloor \tfrac{\ell+1}{2} \right\rfloor}. \] Our approach exploits the free product structure of $\Gamma_{2r}$, together with a combinatorial counting function and recurrence relations arising from cyclically reduced representatives. We further show that the asymptotic growth rate of primitive reciprocal conjugacy classes of word length $\ell$ coincides with that of $\mathcal{N}_\ell$. This result extends previous work for odd values of $p$ and provides a uniform asymptotic bound for all Hecke groups.

papers.title: Representations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and hyperplane complements
papers.abstract: We study faithful realisations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and study Vinberg systems associated to them. We show that they induce embeddings of hyperplane complements, which provide geometrical realisations of certain types of strong admissible (LCM) homomorphisms between Artin--Tits groups.

papers.title: Lipshitz-Sarkar refines mirrors more than Khovanov
papers.abstract: Lipshitz and Sarkar asked in an ICM 2018 question whether their homotopy-theoretic refinement of Khovanov homology can detect mirror reflection when ordinary integral Khovanov homology cannot. We give an affirmative answer by presenting a prime knot whose integral Khovanov homology agrees with that of its mirror in every bidegree, including torsion, and yet over $\mathbb{F}_2$, the second Steenrod square has rank one for the knot and rank zero for its mirror in a specified bidegree. We also give a composite example. The construction, search and computations are done with the help of {\it chat-GTP 5.6 sol Pro} combing over the {\it Regina Census} of knots.

papers.title: Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups
papers.abstract: We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of the generalized cactus group associated with a finite standard parabolic subgroup of the underlying Coxeter group. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types B, D, E, F, and H, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine the associated generalized cactus group directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When the Coxeter diagram has finitely many vertices, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups. In type A, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group on $n$ strands if and only if it embeds into a Sylow 2-subgroup of the symmetric group on $n$ letters. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types A and B and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.
